prs.title: fix(streamable-http): wait for post_writer before yielding
prs.author: Epochex
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Race condition in streamable_http.py's post_writer: the task group starts post_writer with start_soon() and immediately proceeds/yields before post_writer has actually entered its stream context and begun consuming write_stream_reader, which can drop the first message(s) or hang callers under load. members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition in streamable_http.py's post_writer: the task group starts post_writer with start_soon() and immediately proceeds/yields before post_writer has actually entered its stream context and begun consuming write_stream_reader, which can drop the first message(s) or hang callers under load. Both PRs fix this by adding a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to post_writer and calling `task_status.started(None)` once the stream context is entered, so the caller can `tg.start()` it and wait for the readiness signal instead of racing ahead.

members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: Race condition in streamable_http.py's post_writer: the task group starts post_writer with start_soon() and immediately proceeds/yields before post_writer has actually entered its stream context and begun consuming write_stream_reader, which can drop the first message(s) or hang callers under load. Both PRs fix this by adding a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to post_writer and calling `task_status.started(None)` once the stream context is entered, so the caller can `tg.start()` it and wait for the readiness signal instead of racing ahead.

members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: ClientSession's async-context-manager contract isn't enforced: nothing tracks whether __aenter__ has actually run, so misuse (never entering, or entering twice) goes undetected. #1849 adds an `_entered: bool` attribute to ClientSession and raises RuntimeError when the session is used without going through `async with`, which previously caused silent hangs (the background read-loop task was never started). #2631 adds the same-named `self._entered` instance attribute in `__init__` and checks it in `__aenter__`, raising RuntimeError when the session is entered twice. Both patches touch the same class attribute/init region of src/mcp/client/session.py (the `__init__`/`__aenter__` block around line ~351-373) with an identically-named `_entered` flag introduced to fix session lifecycle misuse — they will conflict if merged independently and address the same root cause: unguarded ClientSession entry state. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: 2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` generalizes the fix to any union composed solely of JSON-scalar types (str, int, float, bool, None) — e.g. `str | int`, `str | bool` — not just `Optional[str]`, so it covers strictly more of the corruption cases than 3056's `_is_optional_str`, which only special-cases the None-containing case. 3056's only advantage is explicit `Annotated[...]` unwrapping before the union check, which is a small, easily-portable addition if not already covered; the core fix logic in 2032 is the broader, more complete solution to the same root cause.

members.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
members.author: adityuhkapoor
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both fix the same underlying bug in `pre_parse_json` (src/mcp/server/mcpserver/utilities/func_metadata.py): the function attempts JSON-decoding of string field values whenever the annotation is not exactly `str`, so a union annotation like `str | None` (Optional[str]) causes a valid string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. "123", "null", "[1,2]") to be silently corrupted into an int/None/list instead of being kept as a string. Both PRs add logic to `pre_parse_json`'s gating condition to detect 'str-compatible' union annotations and skip the JSON parse for them. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: 2654 changes the write_stream buffer default from 0 to 1 directly, so the fix applies to every caller without any code changes elsewhere, and it ships a dedicated regression test (BlockingStdout, simulating a slow stdout write) that reproduces the exact blocking scenario and verifies it's resolved. 2215 only adds read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size parameters while leaving both defaults at 0, so the blocking behavior is unchanged for any caller that doesn't explicitly pass a nonzero value — it does not fix the default code path, and its diff shows no equivalent test exercising the blocking/queueing scenario.

clusters.pick_reason: #2478 fixes pickling generically at the MCPError base via a dispatcher (_restore_mcp_error) that covers every subclass, special-casing UrlElicitationRequiredError's from_error path only where needed — so any future MCPError subclass gets pickle-safety for free. #2555 only adds __reduce__ to the one subclass (UrlElicitationRequiredError), leaving every other MCPError subclass with the same unpickling TypeError. #2478 also drops the '# pragma: no cover' on MCPError.data, indicating that code path is now exercised by a test.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the identical lines in RequestResponder.cancel(), so they cannot both merge without conflict. #2493 only deletes the old 'send an error response' code path and leaves server.py's comment/log wording updated, with no replacement behavior for the case where cancellation originates locally (timeout or caller-initiated) rather than from a peer CancelledNotification — the peer is left with neither a response nor a notification in that path. #2514 covers a superset: it imports CancelledNotificationParams and adds logic to emit a proper notifications/cancelled to the peer specifically for the request-timeout and caller-cancellation cases, while still not sending the erroneous response. It also drops a `# pragma: no cover` on the `_entered` check, indicating that branch gained explicit test coverage as part of this PR.
